Macrons

Consonantal i

Clothes & getting dressed

pyjamas noun

also pajamas, pyjama, pajama

our formation

vestis nocturna

pyjamas, nightclothes

The household word, used in the libellī and the Sermō parentis cards. A modern description.

Examples

  • Theodōrus, veste nocturnā etiamtum indūtus, ad mēnsam sedēbat

    Theo, still in his pyjamas, was sitting at the tableLibellus III, Apud avum et aviam

Other words

  • tunica nocturna — pyjama top

    also used · our formation

  • brācae nocturnae — pyjama bottoms

    also used · our formation

  • synthesis dormītōria — pyjamas

    also used · modern · Traupman 117

    Not the household word, and not used in the libellī: classically synthesis is a set of clothes or a loose dinner gown (Mart.).

See also nightclothes.

SourcesLewis & Short: synthesis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 117, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
